newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes steady, volume thin.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes steady, volume thin.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were steady at the close but volume remained thin on lack of buying interest, dealers said.
"There were clearly no buyers in the market as they (the sellers) are quoting much higher than what the buyers want to pay," said a dealer.
Dealers said sellers were asking higher prices despite the weakening of the ringgit in Kuala Lumpur to 2.6250 at 1000 GMT from 2.6175 at 0200 GMT.
"They seem confident that if demand returns, they'll make the money," said a trader.
"That remains to be seen as even short-covering seems to have ceased this week," added the trader.
Dealers said the only inquiries for Malaysian rubber this week were from Chinese dealers checking prices of the SMR20. "They were not buying," said a Malaysian trader.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the RSS1 for August buyers at 248.50 cents (95 U.S. cents) a kg, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
The SMR20 for August buyers was half cent higher at 247.50 cents a kg.
Traders offered the SMR CV at 294 cents, SMR L at 275, SMR 5 at 254, SMR 10 at 248 and SMR 20 at 246. Drum latex was offered at 191 cents.
The INRO's five-day average price was 190.43 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 29, compared to 189.54 on July 28. The daily indicator was 191.91 against 192.76.
Malaysia-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
